question: What was the main goal of the Second Five-Year Plan? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Achieving self-sufficiency in agriculture
Increasing exports
Rapid industrialisation
Improving rural infrastructure
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rapid industrialisation

Explanation:
The main objective of the Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961) was rapid industrialisation, with a special focus on the development of heavy industries. It is also known as the Mahalanobis Plan, named after the eminent statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis. The plan emphasised sectors like steel, coal, electricity and heavy machinery to build a foundation for long-term economic growth. Capital goods were prioritised over agriculture and consumer goods. Under this plan, steel plants were established at Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela.

☛ Other name of Second Five-Year Plan → Mahalanobis Plan
☛ Key sector in Second Five-Year Plan → Heavy industries
☛ Steel plants set up under this plan → Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela
question_hi: द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना का मुख्य लक्ष्य क्या था? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: कृषि में आत्मनिर्भरता प्राप्त करना
निर्यात में वृद्धि करना
तेजी से औद्योगीकरण
ग्रामीण बुनियादी ढाँचे में सुधार
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है तेजी से औद्योगीकरण

Explanation:
द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना (1956-1961) का मुख्य उद्देश्य तेजी से औद्योगीकरण और विशेष रूप से भारी उद्योगों का विकास था। इसे महालनोबिस योजना के नाम से भी जाना जाता है, जिसे प्रसिद्ध सांख्यिकीविद् प्रशांत चंद्र महालनोबिस ने तैयार किया था। इस योजना में स्टील, कोयला, बिजली और भारी मशीनरी जैसे क्षेत्रों पर जोर दिया गया, ताकि दीर्घकालिक आर्थिक विकास की नींव रखी जा सके। कृषि और उपभोक्ता वस्तुओं की तुलना में पूंजीगत वस्तुओं को प्राथमिकता दी गई। इस योजना के तहत भिलाई, दुर्गापुर और राउरकेला में स्टील संयंत्र स्थापित किए गए।

question: Which of the following best describes globalisation? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Isolating economies from global markets
Increasing international interdependence and trade
Reducing international trade
Limiting cultural exchange
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Increasing international interdependence and trade

Explanation:
Globalisation refers to the growing interconnectedness of economies, cultures, and political systems across the world. It is characterized by increased international trade, investment, technology transfer, and cultural exchange. Option 2 accurately describes globalisation as 'increasing international interdependence and trade'. The other options—isolating economies, reducing trade, and limiting cultural exchange—are contrary to the concept of globalisation. Globalisation has led to greater economic integration, with countries relying on each other for goods, services, and capital. This process has been driven by advancements in transportation, communication, and trade liberalization policies. Multinational corporations play a key role in this process by operating across multiple countries. Globalisation also has cultural dimensions, leading to the spread of ideas, values, and practices worldwide.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Key driver of globalisation? → International trade and investment
☛ Multinational corporations → Promote globalisation
☛ WTO → Regulates global trade
☛ Example of cultural globalisation → Spread of fast food and movies
☛ Criticism of globalisation → Rising inequality and cultural homogenisation

Explanation:
वैश्वीकरण से तात्पर्य देशों के बीच बढ़ती आर्थिक, सांस्कृतिक और राजनीतिक अंतर्संबंधों से है। यह अंतर्राष्ट्रीय व्यापार, निवेश, प्रौद्योगिकी हस्तांतरण और सांस्कृतिक आदान-प्रदान को बढ़ावा देता है। विकल्प 2 में दी गई परिभाषा 'बढ़ती अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अन्योन्याश्रयता और व्यापार' वैश्वीकरण के मूलभूत पहलू को सटीक रूप से दर्शाती है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे अर्थव्यवस्थाओं को अलग करना या व्यापार में कमी करना वैश्वीकरण के विपरीत अवधारणाएँ हैं। वैश्वीकरण के कारण देश एक-दूसरे पर अधिक निर्भर हो गए हैं, जिससे वैश्विक आपूर्ति श्रृंखलाएँ और बहुराष्ट्रीय कंपनियों का विस्तार हुआ है।

question: Which organization promotes rural development and self-employment in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)
World Trade Organization (WTO)
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)

Explanation:
NABARD promotes rural development and self-employment in India. It was established in 1982 on the recommendation of the B. Sivaraman Committee. It provides financial support for agriculture and small-scale industries in rural areas. NABARD promotes Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and rural self-employment. Its headquarters is located in Mumbai.

question: What was the role of the public sector in India’s industrial development from 1947 to 1991? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: To promote private investment
To dominate key industries and infrastructure
To support small-scale industries
To focus on export-oriented industries
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To dominate key industries and infrastructure

Explanation:
From 1947 to 1991, India adopted a mixed economy model where the public sector played a leading role in heavy industries and infrastructure. The Industrial Policy Resolutions of 1948 and 1956 placed strategic industries like steel, coal, oil, and transport under the public sector. Public sector undertakings such as SAIL, BHEL, and ONGC drove import substitution and strengthened the industrial base. The goal was economic self-reliance and regional balance, not promoting private investment or focusing on exports.

☛ What was the main objective of the public sector? → Economic self-reliance and infrastructure development
☛ Which plan emphasized heavy industries? → Second Five-Year Plan
☛ SAIL and BHEL belong to which sector? → Public sector
☛ What was the role of the public sector in a mixed economy? → Control over strategic industries
question_hi: 1947 से 1991 तक भारत के औद्योगिक विकास में सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र की क्या भूमिका थी? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)

Solution: सही उत्तर है मुख्य उद्योगों और बुनियादी ढाँचे पर हावी होना

Explanation:
1947 से 1991 तक भारत ने मिश्रित अर्थव्यवस्था मॉडल अपनाया, जिसमें सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र को भारी उद्योगों और बुनियादी ढाँचे में अग्रणी भूमिका दी गई। औद्योगिक नीति प्रस्ताव 1948 और 1956 ने रणनीतिक उद्योगों (जैसे इस्पात, कोयला, तेल, परिवहन) को सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के अधीन रखा। सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के उपक्रम जैसे सेल, बीएचईएल, ओएनजीसी ने आयात प्रतिस्थापन और औद्योगिक आधार को मजबूत किया। इसका उद्देश्य आर्थिक आत्मनिर्भरता और क्षेत्रीय संतुलन था, न कि निजी निवेश को बढ़ावा देना या निर्यात पर ध्यान केंद्रित करना।

question: Which organisation provided financial support to India during the 1991 economic crisis? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: United Nations
International Monetary Fund
Asian Development Bank
World Trade Organization
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is International Monetary Fund

Explanation:
In 1991, India faced a severe economic crisis with foreign exchange reserves falling to just two weeks of imports. To tackle this crisis, the Indian government sought an emergency loan of $2.2 billion from the International Monetary Fund (IMF). In return, the IMF imposed conditions requiring structural reforms, leading to the New Economic Policy of 1991. This policy introduced liberalization, privatization, and globalization (LPG) reforms, which transformed India's economy. The IMF's financial assistance helped India avoid default and set the stage for rapid economic growth in the following decades.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who was the Prime Minister of India during the 1991 economic crisis? → P. V. Narasimha Rao
☛ What policy was implemented by India under IMF loan conditions? → New Economic Policy (LPG)
☛ How much were India's foreign exchange reserves in 1991? → Approximately $1 billion
☛ When was the IMF established? → 1944 (Bretton Woods Conference)
☛ Where is the IMF headquarters located? → Washington D.C., USA
question_hi: 1991 के आर्थिक संकट के दौरान भारत को किस संगठन ने वित्तीय सहायता प्रदान की थी? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 2)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मुद्रा कोष

Explanation:
1991 में भारत गंभीर आर्थिक संकट से जूझ रहा था, जिसमें विदेशी मुद्रा भंडार घटकर केवल दो सप्ताह के आयात के लिए पर्याप्त रह गया था। इस संकट से निपटने के लिए भारत सरकार ने अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मुद्रा कोष (IMF) से 2.2 अरब डॉलर का आपातकालीन ऋण लिया। इस सहायता के बदले IMF ने भारत से संरचनात्मक सुधारों की मांग की, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप 1991 में नई आर्थिक नीति लागू की गई। इस नीति के तहत उदारीकरण, निजीकरण और वैश्वीकरण (LPG) के सुधार किए गए। IMF की सहायता ने भारत को डिफॉल्ट से बचाया और आर्थिक सुधारों की नींव रखी।

question: Who among the following thinkers introduced the Human Development Index for the first time in 1990? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 2)

Explanation:
The Human Development Index (HDI) was first introduced in 1990 by Pakistani economist Mahabub-Ul-Haq. This index measures a country's development using three dimensions: longevity and health, education, and standard of living. It is released annually by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). Mahabub-Ul-Haq believed that development is not merely about income growth but about expanding people's capabilities. His approach revolutionized development economics. HDI is measured on a scale from 0 to 1, where 1 represents the highest human development.

question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the lending rates of scheduled commercial banks (SCBs) in September 2024, in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 2)

The RBI's monthly bulletin publishes these figures, which help assess monetary policy transmission. question: What does globalisation primarily involve? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Integration of the world economy through trade, technology and investment
Isolation of countries from global trade
Restricting foreign goods
Decreasing communication between nations
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Integration of the world economy through trade, technology and investment

Explanation:
Globalisation primarily involves the integration of national economies through increased flows of trade, technology, and investment. This process reduces barriers such as tariffs and quotas, allowing goods, services, capital, and information to move more freely across borders. Key drivers include liberalisation policies, multinational corporations, and digital revolution. Globalisation fosters economic growth and development but also poses challenges like inequality and cultural homogenisation. It creates global supply chains and interdependencies, linking the fate of economies worldwide. The concept emerged prominently in the late 20th century with advances in transportation and communication technologies. Institutions like the WTO facilitate this integration by setting rules for international trade. Globalisation thus transforms how nations interact economically and socially.

question: Which Five-Year Plan emphasised the development of heavy industries and the secondary sector? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Second Five-Year Plan
First Five-Year Plan
Fourth Five-Year Plan
Third Five-Year Plan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Second Five-Year Plan

Explanation:
The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961) emphasised the development of heavy industries and the secondary sector. Also known as the Mahalanobis Plan, after its chief architect Professor Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis, it aimed at rapid industrialisation, focusing on sectors like steel, coal, and heavy machinery. The plan prioritised strengthening the public sector and adopted an import substitution policy. Its target growth rate was 4.5%, but the actual growth was around 4.2%. While it boosted industrial capacity, the neglect of agriculture led to food shortages in later years. This plan laid the foundation for India's industrial base and is considered a landmark in India's economic planning.

Solution: Correct Answer is Dadabhai Naoroji

Explanation:
The 'Drain Theory' was popularised by Dadabhai Naoroji in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901). This theory argued that British rule systematically drained wealth from India to Britain, leading to India's impoverishment. Naoroji used statistical data to show how British policies caused economic exploitation. He was the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament. He estimated India's national income and proved that a large portion of India's wealth was being transferred to England. This theory became a cornerstone of Indian economic nationalism. Naoroji's works highlighted the structural exploitation of India under colonialism, influencing many freedom fighters. The drain theory remains a key concept in understanding colonial economic history.

question: What is the relationship between poverty and unemployment? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Unemployment leads to wealth redistribution.
Unemployment often leads to higher poverty levels due to lack
Poverty reduces unemployment.
Poverty and unemployment are unrelated.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Unemployment often leads to higher poverty levels due to lack

Explanation:
The relationship between poverty and unemployment is direct and cyclical. Unemployment results in a lack of income, pushing individuals below the poverty line as they cannot afford basic necessities. Conversely, poverty limits access to education and skills, reducing employability and perpetuating unemployment. This creates a vicious cycle where each condition reinforces the other. Governments aim to break this cycle through policies like job creation and skill development programs. Therefore, unemployment is a major cause of poverty, and poverty contributes to sustained unemployment.

☛ What is the main cause of poverty? → Unemployment and income inequality.
☛ What is the relationship between unemployment and poverty called? → Vicious cycle.
☛ How is poverty line determined in India? → Based on minimum calorie intake and income level.
☛ How many types of unemployment are there? → Cyclical, structural, frictional, and seasonal.
☛ Which organization measures unemployment in India? → National Sample Survey Office (NSSO).

question: What is globalisation? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: A political alliance between countries
Integration of economies worldwide
Decline in international trade
An increase in cultural isolation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Integration of economies worldwide

Explanation:
Globalisation refers to the increasing interconnectedness and integration of economies, cultures, and societies across the world. It is primarily driven by international trade, foreign investment, technology, and the flow of information. This process involves increased cross-border transactions and global supply chains. Globalisation has led to greater economic integration, facilitating the movement of goods, services, capital, and labour. In contrast, a political alliance, decline in international trade, or increase in cultural isolation do not define globalisation. Understanding this concept is crucial for comprehending modern world dynamics.

question: According to the Gandhian view of Development, which of the following is the focal point of economic development? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Family
Individual
Government
Village
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Village

Explanation:
According to the Gandhian view of development, the focal point of economic development is the village. Mahatma Gandhi believed that the soul of India resides in its villages, so development should be village-centric. He proposed the concept of Gram Swaraj (village self-rule), where each village is a self-sufficient unit. Gandhi emphasized decentralization, local resource utilization, and small-scale industries. He was opposed to large-scale industrialization and urbanization. According to him, true development can only occur when villages are economically uplifted and become self-reliant. Gandhi also stressed Antyodaya (the upliftment of the poorest person).

question: One of the primary goals of the New Economic Policy of 1991 was to control which of the following? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Regional imbalances
Population growth
Environmental issues
Inflation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Inflation

Explanation:
The primary goal of the New Economic Policy of 1991 was to control inflation. India was facing a severe balance of payments crisis and inflation had soared above 12%. The policy introduced fiscal discipline, monetary contraction, and reduced direct taxes. The RBI increased CRR and bank rate to tighten money supply. Under Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG), price stability was prioritized. The policy abolished industrial licensing and cut import duties to boost competition, which helped curb inflation. These measures stabilized the economy and paved the way for higher growth.

question: Every year, the Human Development Index is released by ________. (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 1)

World Health Organization
UNICEF
solution:

Explanation:

It measures a country's development based on three dimensions: long and healthy life (life expectancy at birth), education (mean and expected years of schooling), and standard of living (gross national income per capita). The UNDP has published the Human Development Report since 1990. HDI classifies countries into very high, high, medium, and low human development categories. In the 2024 report, Switzerland ranked first, while India ranked 134th.

question: What role did the Minimum Support Price play in agriculture post the 1991 reforms? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 1)

It was abolished entirely
It was replaced by international pricing policies.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It continued to protect farmers from price fluctuations

Explanation:
Even after the 1991 economic reforms, the Minimum Support Price (MSP) remained a crucial policy instrument. The reforms aimed to move towards a market-based economy, but in agriculture, MSP was retained to protect farmers from price fluctuations. The government guarantees a minimum price for crops, ensuring income stability and shielding farmers from market uncertainties. MSP was neither abolished nor replaced; instead, its scope was expanded, covering major crops like rice and wheat. Although reforms liberalised agricultural trade, MSP continued to be the cornerstone of food security and farmer welfare. Thus, MSP continued its role of protecting farmers from price risks.

question: Which of the following best describes the concept of offshoring? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Transferring certain company tasks or services to a foreign country to lower expenses
Hiring temporary workers for short-term projects
Relocating business operations to another area within the same country
Decreasing wages within the company to boost profits
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Transferring certain company tasks or services to a foreign country to lower expenses

Explanation:
Offshoring refers to the practice of transferring specific business tasks or services to a foreign country, primarily to reduce costs such as labor, taxes, or other operational expenses. The company retains ownership and control but relocates operations abroad. This differs from outsourcing, which involves contracting tasks to a third party, domestic or foreign. Options like hiring temporary workers, relocating within the same country, or decreasing wages do not represent offshoring. Offshoring is a key aspect of globalization, enabling companies to leverage global efficiencies.

question: The concept of a Five Year Plan was inspired by which country? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: France
Soviet Union
United Kingdom
United States
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Soviet Union

Explanation:
The concept of Five Year Plans in India was inspired by the Soviet Union (USSR). The Soviet Union implemented its first Five Year Plan in 1928, focusing on rapid industrialization and agricultural collectivization. India, under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru, adopted this model and launched its first Five Year Plan in 1951. The plan emphasized agriculture, irrigation, and energy sectors. The Soviet model influenced India's mixed economy approach and the dominant role of the public sector in economic development.

question: Which term describes the removal of restrictions on private industries in the 1991 reforms? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Liberalisation
Privatisation
Globalisation
Industrialisation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Liberalisation

Explanation:
In the 1991 economic reforms, Liberalisation refers to the removal of restrictions on private industries. It included abolishing the license raj, eliminating the requirement for prior approval to set up industries, and promoting foreign investment. Liberalisation made the Indian economy more market-oriented and encouraged competition. Privatisation involves transferring public sector enterprises to private ownership, while Globalisation means opening the economy to international trade and investment. Liberalisation played a key role in rescuing India from the economic crisis of 1990-91, leading to higher growth and efficiency.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ What happens in privatisation? → Transfer of government enterprises to private hands
☛ Main objective of globalisation? → Increase international trade and investment
☛ Three pillars of 1991 reforms? → Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation
☛ Meaning of industrialisation? → Expansion and development of industries
question_hi: 1991 के सुधारों में निजी उद्योगों पर लगे प्रतिबंधों को हटाने के लिए किस शब्द का प्रयोग किया जाता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)

निजीकरण
वैश्वीकरण

Explanation:

question: What was the primary reason for the failure of India’s Third Five Year Plan? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Global recession
Oil crisis
Indo-China war of 1962
Indo-Pak war of 1965 and drought
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indo-Pak war of 1965 and drought

Explanation:
The primary reason for the failure of India's Third Five Year Plan (1961-1966) was the Indo-Pak war of 1965 and a severe drought. The war diverted substantial funds to defense, reducing resources for development. Consecutive droughts in 1965 and 1966 caused a sharp decline in agricultural output, leading to food shortages and inflation. Foreign exchange reserves dwindled, and industrial production was also hampered. The target growth rate of 5.6% could not be achieved; the actual growth rate was only about 2.5%. This failure led to a plan holiday (1966-69) and a shift in focus towards agriculture and price stability.

☛ Main objective → Self-reliance in agriculture and industry
☛ War responsible for failure → Indo-Pak war of 1965
☛ Natural calamity → Severe drought of 1965-66
☛ Actual growth rate → 2.5% (target 5.6%)
question_hi: भारत की तीसरी पंचवर्षीय योजना की विफलता का प्राथमिक कारण क्या था? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: वैश्विक मंदी
तेल संकट
1962 का भारत-चीन युद्ध
1965 का भारत-पाक युद्ध और सूखा
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 1965 का भारत-पाक युद्ध और सूखा

Explanation:
भारत की तीसरी पंचवर्षीय योजना (1961-1966) का मुख्य लक्ष्य कृषि और उद्योग में आत्मनिर्भरता प्राप्त करना था। इस योजना की विफलता का प्राथमिक कारण 1965 का भारत-पाक युद्ध और भीषण सूखा था। युद्ध के कारण रक्षा पर भारी व्यय हुआ, जिससे विकास निधि में कमी आई। लगातार दो वर्षों (1965-66) के सूखे ने कृषि उत्पादन को बुरी तरह प्रभावित किया, जिससे खाद्यान्न संकट और मुद्रास्फीति बढ़ी। विदेशी मुद्रा भंडार में गिरावट आई और औद्योगिक उत्पादन भी प्रभावित हुआ। योजना का विकास दर लक्ष्य 5.6% था, जो केवल 2.5% रह गया। इस असफलता के बाद योजना अवकाश (1966-69) की घोषणा की गई।
